domain_setting: A contemporary school and university learning environment: quiet library desks, lively classrooms, lecturer consultation, student services, and assessment spaces.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use student desks, plain books, blank papers, and varied age-appropriate learners as scale cues.
Use the shared school palette of pale paper, slate blue, sage green, warm coral, and muted gold.
Never put legible letters, words, numerals, charts, or symbols in the illustration; ideas must be shown with shapes, objects, and body language.
Keep important figures and props large enough to read at the vocabulary card size, comfortably within the 304 by 192 viewBox.

polysemy_resolution_table.assignment: A school or university task set for a learner, not a job duty in the workplace.
polysemy_resolution_table.office hours: A teacher's scheduled time for student consultation, not general business opening hours.
polysemy_resolution_table.practice: Repeated rehearsal to improve a learned skill, represented by deliberate musical instrument practice rather than generic studying.
polysemy_resolution_table.presentation: An oral academic report delivered to a small audience, not the act of presenting a gift.
polysemy_resolution_table.review: Looking back over previously learned material, distinct from giving feedback or grading another person's work.
polysemy_resolution_table.study / studying: General learning activity in a school or library setting, rather than the act of studying one named subject.
polysemy_resolution_table.degree (qualification): A university qualification, distinguished from the verb phrase get a degree by showing the awarded credential itself.
polysemy_resolution_table.fresher: A first-year university student, especially in British usage, not someone who has just refreshed something.
polysemy_resolution_table.freshman: A first-year high-school or university student, especially in American usage; visually distinct from fresher by campus orientation details rather than nationality stereotypes.
polysemy_resolution_table.postgraduate: A learner studying beyond an undergraduate degree, shown in advanced research work.
polysemy_resolution_table.semester: One half-year teaching period in a two-semester academic year.
polysemy_resolution_table.take a year off / take a year out: A planned gap in formal study before returning, using two regional phrasings for the same concept; show travel or purposeful experience between academic periods.
polysemy_resolution_table.term: A school or university teaching period, despite the general dictionary sense of a technical word.
polysemy_resolution_table.undergraduate: A university student pursuing a first degree, distinguished from postgraduate study by course level and research setting.
polysemy_resolution_table.continuous assessment: Progress measured through several assignments and quizzes across a course, rather than one final exam.
polysemy_resolution_table.feedback: Constructive comments that help a learner improve work, not electronic signal feedback.
polysemy_resolution_table.get a degree: The action of receiving a completed university qualification, shown as a student accepting a diploma at graduation.
polysemy_resolution_table.graduate: A person who has completed university, not the act of graduating; distinct from the action get a degree.
polysemy_resolution_table.give someone feedback on something: An instructor or peer gives specific helpful comments on another learner's work.
polysemy_resolution_table.deadline: The due-by point for submitting an assignment, represented without a written date or numerals.
polysemy_resolution_table.meet a deadline / miss a deadline: Paired outcomes: submit the finished work before the due moment versus arrive after it has passed.
polysemy_resolution_table.pass with flying colors: Achieve a notably strong result, conveyed by an excellent paper and celebratory motion without letters, numbers, or marks.
polysemy_resolution_table.quiz: A short informal classroom check, distinct from the action of taking a test or a formal exam.
polysemy_resolution_table.take a test: A learner actively answers a short assessment, distinct from the test paper as an object and the more formal take an exam.
polysemy_resolution_table.take an exam: A learner actively completes a formal examination under quiet supervised conditions.
polysemy_resolution_table.clear distinction: Two items or categories separated by an unmistakable visible boundary.
polysemy_resolution_table.compare and contrast: A learner examines two things together, noticing both a shared feature and their differences.
polysemy_resolution_table.polar opposites: Two concepts at the far ends of a continuous contrast, shown at opposite ends of a balanced scale.
polysemy_resolution_table.strikingly different: Two sharply contrasting examples that look immediately unlike one another, emphasized by composition and color.

contrast_notes.assignment / first draft / research / pr: Assignment is the task; first draft is an early incomplete manuscript; research gathers source evidence; presentation is a learner addressing an audience.
contrast_notes.memorize / practice / review / study / s: Memorize uses recall cues; practice shows repeated skill rehearsal; review rereads old material; study is the general activity; studying is the ongoing activity; take notes records key points while listening.
contrast_notes.fresher / freshman / undergraduate / pos: Fresher and freshman are distinct regional labels for first-year students; undergraduate is the broader first-degree student level; postgraduate is advanced study after a first degree.
contrast_notes.degree / get a degree / graduate: Degree is the academic qualification, get a degree is receiving it, and graduate is the person who has completed the course.
contrast_notes.semester / term: Semester is a half-year academic period; term is a school teaching period and may be shorter or organized differently.
contrast_notes.continuous assessment / quiz / take a te: Continuous assessment accumulates results over time; quiz is a short assessment; take a test shows answering a brief paper; take an exam shows formal supervised examination.
contrast_notes.feedback / give someone feedback on some: Feedback is constructive guidance as an object or concept; give someone feedback shows one person responding to another's specific work.
contrast_notes.deadline / meet a deadline / miss a dead: Deadline is the due point itself; meet shows timely submission; miss shows late arrival after the point has passed.
contrast_notes.clear distinction / compare and contrast: Distinction isolates a boundary; compare and contrast analyzes similarities and differences together; polar opposites occupy two endpoints; strikingly different uses an immediate vivid contrast.
